text:
Utah comes in off a 6-3 loss at Philadelphia on Sunday, its third defeat in five, and is playing without defenseman John Marino. Toronto won 4-2 at Vancouver three days ago, but is missing John Tavares and Kirill Marchenko. The Leafs won the Oct. 13 meeting 5-4 over Utah, though Utah earned the better of the chances that night.

The underlying numbers lean toward Utah. At five on five, the Mammoth have taken 58% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to Toronto's 46%. Toronto's results are ahead of its chances, helped by finishing and goaltending, and it takes 4.6 penalties a game. Our model has Utah scoring 3.52 goals tonight to Toronto's 2.97.

In net, projected starter Sebastian Cossa is 2.7 goals saved above expected below average this season, while Sergei Bobrovsky is slightly positive at +0.9, though he was at -13.5 last season. Cossa has no NHL games last season.

Logan Cooley is worth watching: he had a hat trick in his hometown last week, and we have him at 36% to score and 67% for a point. For Toronto, Auston Matthews carries a four-game point streak and sits at 38% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Anders Lee, a fourth-liner who has made the most of limited minutes, with 3.5 expected goals in his last 10 games. We have him at 22% to score against a Toronto team that gives up plenty of chances.
